Excursions had been operating from Nesquehoning, Pa., since Nov. 2, after a rockslide closed a highway and blocked the R&N rail line below on Oct. 31. [See “Reading & Northern excursion route shut down …,” Trains.com, Nov. 1, 2026]. The move comes on the final day of the Lehigh Gorge Scenic’s “Autumn Leaf” schedule. The railroad returns to its regular schedule on Monday, Nov. 16; that schedule will continue through Thursday, Nov. 26. More information is available on the Lehigh Gorge Scenic website. While the railroad is back in operation, U.S. Route 209 is still closed and expected to remain that way for another six to eight weeks, according to the news site Lehigh Valley Live. candidates.title: Shandong Marine launches new China–South Korea container service
candidates.excerpt: Shandong Marine Corporation (SMC) has launched a new container shipping service connecting Rizhao in China’s Shandong Province with Incheon in South Korea, strengthening maritime links between the two countries. The new Rizhao–Incheon Express (RIX) commenced operations on 11 November 2026, offering two sailings per week with a single container vessel of approximately 1,100 TEU. The service operates on a direct rotation between Rizhao and Incheon, calling at Sun Kwang New Container Terminal (SNCT) at Incheon New Port. According to the Incheon Port Authority, the new connection is expected to reduce transportation times and logistics costs between southern Shandong Province and the Seoul metropolitan area. The port authority estimates that the route could generate approximately 120,000 TEU in additional annual container traffic. candidates.title: Medkon adds Algiers to Turkey–North Africa service
candidates.excerpt: Medkon Lines has expanded its Turkey–North Africa (TNA) service with the addition of a port call at Algiers, extending the service’s coverage to Algeria alongside its existing connection with Tunisia. According to DynaLiners, the revised service will be operated by a single container vessel with a capacity of approximately 700 TEU, offering sailings every 20 days between Turkey and North Africa. The updated port rotation will be: Istanbul (Ambarli) – Izmit (Yilport) – Aliaga – Algiers – Rades – Istanbul (Ambarli). The addition of Algiers provides another direct connection between Turkish ports and Algeria, while maintaining the service’s existing call at Rades in Tunisia. Medkon already serves the Algerian market through its Turkey–Alger (TAE) service. The latest adjustment therefore expands the company’s coverage of Algeria through the TNA rotation rather than marking its entry into the market. candidates.title: Samskip introduces Morocco–North Europe service via Spain
candidates.excerpt: Samskip has introduced a weekly container shipping service connecting Morocco with the Iberian Peninsula and Northern Europe, targeting demand during the Moroccan fruit export season. The service links Agadir with Cádiz and Santander in Spain, Thamesport in the United Kingdom and Rotterdam in the Netherlands, providing connections between Moroccan exporters and European markets. The new rotation will be: Agadir – Cádiz – Santander – Thamesport – Rotterdam – Agadir. Three container vessels, each with a capacity of approximately 1,000 TEU, will be deployed to maintain the weekly service. The inclusion of Cádiz and Santander extends Samskip’s Morocco–Europe maritime connections through the Iberian Peninsula, adding Spanish port coverage alongside its established links with the United Kingdom and the Netherlands. candidates.title: From ocean liner to artificial reef: A warning for container shipping
candidates.excerpt: From ocean liner to artificial reef: A warning for container shipping Dr Raymon Krishnan, president of Singapore’s Logistics & Supply Chain Management Society, writes for Splash today, reflecting on one of this week’s most talked about stories in the mainstream press. On Wednesday, the 990-foot ocean liner SS United States was deliberately sunk off Destin, Florida, to become what is expected to be the world’s largest artificial reef. Initial underwater inspections found the vessel upright, approximately 180 feet below the surface. The sinking of the SS United States reminds us that ships can outlive their commercial purpose. Launched in 1951 and entering service in 1952, the SS United States was the pinnacle of post-war American maritime engineering. It held the record as the world’s fastest passenger ship but was withdrawn in 1969 as commercial aviation transformed the economics of transatlantic travel. candidates.excerpt: Genesee & Wyoming Inc. is planning to separate into three rail holding companies, effective Jan. 1, 2027, a move that will position the regional entities for eventual sale. The companies will continue to be owned by G&W parent Brookfield and GIC. G&W operates more than 100 railroads. The new companies are: Atlantic & Great Lakes Transportation Inc., which will be made up of G&W operations in New England (including Berkshire & Eastern Railroad), New York, Ohio, and Pennsylvania. Atlantic & Great Lakes will be based in Rochester, N.Y., and led by Chief Executive Bill Keough, who has been with G&W for eight years and most recently served as regional senior vice president. Canyon & Cascade Transportation Inc., which will be comprised of G&W operations in Washington, Oregon, California, Arizona, and New Mexico. candidates.excerpt: Rail traffic among U.S. carriers rose 6.6% in the week ending Nov. 7 compared with the same week a year ago, driven by an 11% increase in intermodal shipments, the Association of American Railroads said. Carloads increased 1.3% from a year earlier. Seven of the 10 commodity groups recorded gains, led by motor vehicles and parts, up 10.4%, and forest products, up 10.1%. Metallic ores and metals followed with a 6.4% increase. Grain shipments declined 2.4%, nonmetallic minerals fell 1.7%, and coal slipped 1.2% among weaker volumes. Through the first 44 weeks of 2026, total U.S. rail traffic increased 3.9% compared with the same period in 2025. Intermodal volume rose 4.9%, carloads increased 2.7%. Grain remained the strongest-growing freight category year to date, up 9.7%, despite its weekly decline. Metallic ores and metals increased 8.8%, and petroleum and petroleum products rose 7.7%. Total carloads for the week ending October 31 were 233,816 carloads, up 3.0 percent compared with the same week in 2025, while U.S. weekly intermodal volume was 280,264 containers and trailers, up 3.9 percent compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. They included metallic ores and metals, up 3,883 carloads, to 25,059; chemicals, up 2,542 carloads, to 34,523; and motor vehicles and parts, up 1,351 carloads, to 16,268. Commodity groups that posted decreases compared with the same week in 2025 were grain, down 2,092 carloads, to 23,078; miscellaneous carloads, down 1,162 carloads, to 8,369; and coal, down 224 carloads, to 55,042.
